turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning, I'm Sister Jacobs. Vitals first: blood pressure one forty-two over eighty-eight, pulse seventy-six, temperature thirty-six point eight, oxygen ninety-eight percent.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come through, have a seat. Doctor Naidoo. What brings you in?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Toe.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Which toe, what's wrong with it?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Big one. Sore.
[SEG0006] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Right big toe, doctor. Swollen right up since last night, he didn't sleep a wink.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Since last night?
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja.
[SEG0009] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He was limping already at yesterday's braai, mid-afternoon, mind you.
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): Night.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, last night it is, from you. Out of ten, how sore?
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): Nine. Throbbing.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Can you walk on it?
[SEG0014] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. He hopped from the bakkie and wouldn't put the foot down.
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): Walked.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): You actually walked?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja.
[SEG0018] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Barely. I'm standing right here.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll record that you disagree. Any fever, or feeling ill in yourself?
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Did you injure it? Stub the toe, drop something?
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0023] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Wait, though. He was shifting the braai chairs and there was a bang.
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): Chair.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Kicked a chair?
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja. Last night.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Has the same thing happened before?
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): When?
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): Year.
[SEG0031] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): About a year back, same right toe, sore and swollen, faded after a few days. We never came to the rooms.
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Are you on any tablets?
[SEG0034] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Just the water tablet. Hydrochlorothiazide, for his blood pressure, twenty-five milligrams every morning. I think that's the dose.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Twenty-five milligrams every morning, yes?
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja.
[SEG0037] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He takes it daily, I set it out with the coffee. No skipping.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicine?
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Beer?
[SEG0041] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Weekends, ja. A six-pack of Castle at the braai, Saturdays, sometimes Sunday too.
[SEG0042] person_3 (PATIENT): Two.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Two beers on the weekend, not a six-pack?
[SEG0044] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja.
[SEG0045] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ag, alright, I stretched it. Parking was a nightmare as well, we nearly went home.
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mondays, hey. Let me see that foot.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right big toe joint is swollen, red and hot, exquisitely tender. No break in the skin. Calf is soft and cool.

[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sudden pain in that joint, weekend beer, a thiazide, same episode a year ago. I'm leaning toward gout, but I will not conclude that yet. Infection in the joint is still possible, and so is irritation from the kick to the chair. The bloods won't wrap it up by themselves either.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll order a serum uric acid today. Holding off on an X-ray.
[SEG0050] person_1 (NURSE): I can take the blood just now when you're done, doctor.

[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): I could treat this with colchicine or with an anti-inflammatory such as naproxen. We'll use colchicine, nought point five milligrams by mouth, two tablets now, one tablet an hour later, then one tablet twice a day for three days. Naproxen stays off unless I say otherwise. If you get bad diarrhoea, stop the colchicine and phone the rooms before any anti-inflammatory is added.

[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): Keep taking the hydrochlorothiazide. Give the beer a skip this weekend, foot up on a cushion. Come back in three days, and sooner if there's a fever or red streaks running up the leg.
[SEG0053] person_3 (PATIENT): Fine.
[SEG0054] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Righto, chemist on the way home. Thanks, doctor.
